title: They didn’t just mock Him…
paragraphs: They didn’t just mock Him…
they crowned Him.

Not with gold.
Not with honor.
Not with anything worthy of a King.

They took thorns—
sharp, cursed, brutal thorns—
twisted them together,
and forced them onto His head.
Not gently.
But violently.

Until they pierced skin…
until blood ran down His face…
until pain became visible.
And yet—He didn’t resist.
Here’s what most people miss:
The crown of thorns was not random.
It was deeply symbolic.

Because thorns were first mentioned in Genesis 3:18,
when sin entered the world.
"The ground will produce thorns and thistles for you…"
Thorns were a sign of the curse.
A visible reminder that something had gone wrong between God and man.

So when Jesus stood there—
bleeding under a crown of thorns—
this was not just cruelty.
This was substitution.

What began in a garden with Adam…
was now being answered by Jesus.

The first Adam chose disobedience
and brought the curse.

The second Adam chose obedience
and carried the curse.
And where did the curse rest?
On His head.
Let that sink in.

The very place where authority sits…
the very place where identity is declared…
was covered in pain.
Because Jesus was not just suffering physically.
He was wearing what belonged to us.
He wore the crown of our curse.
Every thorn represented something:

Your sin.
Your guilt.
Your shame.
Your hidden battles.
Your silent struggles.
Your consequences.
Pressed into Him.

Not symbolically—
but sacrificially.
And here’s the tension:
They were mocking Him as a King…
"Hail, King of the Jews!"

They laughed.
They struck Him.
They spat on Him.
But heaven wasn’t laughing.
Because while they thought it was a joke—
they were crowning the true King.
The crown didn’t prove He wasn’t a King.
It proved what kind of King He is.

Not one who avoids pain.
But one who enters it.

Not one who demands honor.
But one who absorbs humiliation.
Not one who saves Himself.
But one who chooses to save you.
And maybe that’s where this becomes personal.
Because we all know what it feels like to live among thorns.

Stress that won’t leave.
Regret that won’t fade.
Battles no one else sees.
Cycles we keep repeating.
Life under the curse feels heavy.
And if we’re honest—
sometimes it feels like we’re still wearing it.
But the crown of thorns tells a different story.

Jesus stepped into the curse
so you wouldn’t have to stay in it.
He didn’t remove the thorns from the world—
He took their power over your identity.

You are not what pierced you.
You are not what broke you.
You are not what shamed you.
Because He already carried it.
The crown was never the end of the story.
There is another crown.
Not made of thorns—
but promised in glory.
James 1:12 calls it “the crown of life.”
And here’s the exchange:

He wore the crown of suffering…
so you could receive the crown of life.
Read that again.
Slowly.

He wore what you deserved
so you could receive what you didn’t earn.
This is not just theology.
This is transformation.
Because when you understand what He carried…
you stop trying to carry it alone.

So the next time life feels heavy—
the next time the “thorns” press in—
remember this:

The curse touched His head
so it wouldn’t define your life.
And maybe the real question isn’t:
“Why did He wear it?”
Maybe the real question is:
“Why are we still carrying what He already took?”
Let this settle in your spirit:

You don’t have to live crowned by pain
when Jesus already wore it for you.

Engagement Question:
What is one “thorn” in your life that you need to finally release to God today?
